Akash Network selects Solana for blockchain migration

Akash Network said it has selected Solana as the destination for its planned blockchain migration. The decentralized GPU and AI compute network currently runs its own Cosmos SDK-based chain, but previously said it intends to move to a shared-security architecture to reduce network maintenance costs and the capital burden associated with AKT staking. Solana and Ethereum had both been under consideration before Akash made its final choice. — link

Galaxy: Bitcoin bear market ended in June, accumulation phase underway

Galaxy Research said Bitcoin’s bear market ended in June 2026 and the asset is now in an accumulation phase, with BTC closing above its 50-week moving average for five consecutive weeks. Monthly transfers from coins held for more than five years have fallen to about 34,000 BTC from 67,000 in 2024, suggesting reduced selling pressure from long-term holders. Galaxy said the bullish view would weaken if Bitcoin falls below its roughly $76,540 50-week moving average and fails to reclaim it within a month. — link

S&P Global acquires OpenZeppelin to boost digital asset risk capabilities

S&P Global has completed its acquisition of blockchain security firm OpenZeppelin for an undisclosed amount. The deal is intended to strengthen S&P Global’s digital asset and smart contract risk capabilities. OpenZeppelin will continue to operate independently under founder Demian Brener, while its open-source smart contract libraries will remain freely available. — link

BitMine said it acquired 10,452 ETH over the past week, bringing total holdings to 6,051,933 ETH, or about 4.95% of Ethereum’s supply. The company also repurchased 2.04 million shares at an average price of $22.48; its 2026 buybacks now total 22.9 million shares, or about $399.6 million. MEXC Lacks MiCA Authorization, Winds Down Netherlands as Restricted-Market List Expands

MEXC said it does not hold MiCA authorization in the EU and EEA and is winding down services in the Netherlands, with final offboarding scheduled for November 16. The exchange is also discontinuing services for users in Russia and Belarus. Separately, its User Agreement currently lists 13 prohibited jurisdictions, including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Singapore, Hong Kong, Mainland China, Malaysia and Kazakhstan. — link

CZ responds to BNB Chain’s updated New L1 plans: “Multiple chains, one coins.” According to BNB Chain docs updated on Oct 22, the new L1 (name TBD) will run in parallel with BSC via a native bridge and will not issue a separate token. It continues using BNB for gas, staking, and governance. Target specs include ~200ms blocks and ~20ms pre-confirmation. An internal multi-validator devnet is already running; public testnet is planned for end of 2026 and mainnet for early 2027. — link
